    Research & Corpus Data Use Statement (Version 1.0)

    Last updated: 20/02/2026

    1. Purpose of This Statement

    This Research & Corpus Data Use Statement explains:

    • what learner‑generated data may be used for research and development,
    • how it is anonymised or pseudonymised,
    • what protections we apply,
    • how consent works, and
    • how you can control or opt out of research use.

    This Statement applies to all products in the &Improve family (Write & Improve, Speak & Improve and Read & Improve).

    It should be read alongside: the Privacy Policy and Terms of Use & Conditions:

    👉 Privacy Policy

    👉 Terms of Use & Conditions

    2. What Research Use Means

    “Research use” refers to the processing of learner‑generated content to:

    • improve automated feedback systems (writing, speaking, reading)
    • develop and evaluate AI‑based language‑learning models
    • benchmark system accuracy
    • understand language‑learning patterns at scale
    • enhance teaching and assessment methods

    Research use does not include:

    • marketing or advertising
    • profiling for non‑educational purposes
    • selling data
    • sharing identifiable data without a lawful basis

    3. What Learner Data May Be Used

    We may use the following learner‑generated content for research.

    3.1 Writing Submissions

    Texts submitted for feedback or assessment, such as paragraphs or essays.

    3.2 Speaking Samples

    Audio recordings provided during speaking tasks or complete tests.

    3.3 Reading Responses

    Typed summaries as reading comprehension tasks.

    3.4 System‑Generated Metadata

    • error types and frequencies
    • feedback categories
    • CEFR‑related performance scores
    • timestamps and task‑interaction patterns

    We do not use account identity data (such as name or email) as part of the research corpus.

    4. How We Protect Your Identity

    We apply layered safeguards to reduce the likelihood that individuals can be identified in research corpora derived from our learning services. These measures differ by data type due to the inherent characteristics of text versus speech. The protections below apply to datasets we prepare for research use and, where indicated, for any public corpus releases.

    4.1 Writing Submissions (Write & Improve)

    4.1.1 Preventive and editorial controls.
    We design prompts to avoid eliciting personal information and apply human review to the first and final versions of each essay set. Sets that include personal data or inappropriate content are removed from corpus preparation. Automated checks (e.g., named‑entity detection) are then used on remaining texts to help identify personal names and locations for further review or removal.

    4.1.2 Pseudonymisation of names (where appropriate).
    Where personal names appear and are not those of widely recognisable public figures, we replace at least one component with an alternative while preserving broad linguistic characteristics to maintain research utility and reduce identifiability.

    4.1.3 Content sanitisation.
    We screen for offensive or triggering language and remove or edit passages where required to align with our safety standards.

    4.1.4 De‑linking of system identifiers.
    Internal platform identifiers are not released. We generate new public identifiers for essays, users and prompts that are unique within the corpus but cannot be used to retrieve account‑level data.

    4.2 Speaking Submissions (Speak & Improve)

    4.2.1 Removal of identity‑prone prompts.
    The first two introductory questions in the speaking test, which may elicit personal identity information, are excluded from the corpus and not scored.

    4.2.2 Quality and suitability filtering.
    Submissions with poor audio quality, meaningless responses, or inappropriate content are excluded during initial review.

    4.2.3 Annotation‑stage exclusions.
    During transcription and grammatical‑error annotation, certain phrases (e.g., those containing unknown words, foreign proper nouns, or code‑switched elements) are excluded from final error‑annotated materials to support accuracy and consistency.

    4.2.4 Nature of the released materials.
    The corpus includes single‑channel 16kHz audio files and associated annotations. —

    4.3 Lawfulness, Transparency & Purpose Limitation

    We process learner submissions for research and product improvement purposes as described in this Policy. For research corpora, we apply proportionate safeguards and minimise the scope of data released externally. Where public corpus releases are contemplated, we assess legal bases and apply additional controls as appropriate.

    4.4 Access Controls & Governance

    Where full anonymisation cannot be assured, we prefer controlled access over open publication. This may include researcher applications, non‑commercial licence terms, prohibitions on re‑identification, and takedown pathways. We also operate versioning and correction processes where practicable.

    4.5 Residual Risk & Limitations (Important Notice)

    No combination of technical and organisational measures can guarantee that re‑identification risk is reduced to zero, particularly for audio data. For writing, residual risk primarily concerns undetected indirect identifiers within free text. For speaking, residual risk includes the inherent identifiability of voice and spontaneous disclosure of personal information. We therefore (i) avoid identity‑prone prompts, (ii) remove unsuitable materials, (iii) exclude certain phrase types during annotation, and (iv) prefer pseudonymised textual identifiers and controlled access models where appropriate.

    4.6 Contact & Requests

    Data subjects may contact us with questions about these protections, to request access or objection in accordance with applicable law, or to seek removal of content from a released corpus where identification concerns arise. We will review such requests in light of legal obligations and research integrity considerations.

    5. Lawful Basis for Research Use

    Lawful Basis for Processing Research Data

    We process personal data for research purposes on the basis of Article 6(1)(e) UK GDPR (performance of a task carried out in the public interest), supported where appropriate by Article 6(1)(f) (legitimate interests). Cambridge University Press & Assessment is an exempt charity whose mission includes advancing education, scholarship and research. These activities constitute tasks carried out in the public interest and provide a clear lawful basis for the creation and analysis of research datasets. (Charitable status does not exempt us from UK GDPR obligations; a lawful basis remains required.)

    Where research involves special category data, such as biometric data contained in learner speech recordings, we rely on Article 9(2)(j) UK GDPR and Schedule 1, Part 1(4) of the Data Protection Act 2018, which permit processing necessary for scientific research purposes subject to appropriate safeguards. These safeguards include data minimisation, pseudonymisation where possible, access restrictions, and governance controls appropriate to the sensitivity and potential identifiability of the data.

    We do not normally rely on consent as the lawful basis for processing research data. While obtaining consent may play an important ethical role, it is generally not the appropriate lawful basis for research processing under UK GDPR because consent must be freely given, specific, and withdrawable, which is incompatible with long‑term or public research datasets once released.

    6. Children and Research Use

    For users under the required age for independent consent (e.g., under 13), we require:

    • parental or guardian approval for any research use
    • age‑appropriate restrictions and safeguards
    • the ability for a parent or guardian to withdraw consent at any time

    Children’s data is subject to additional retention limits and stricter access controls.

    We do not include any content generated by minors in our publicly released research datasets.
    Where a learner is identified as a child user, their submissions are excluded from all dataset releases that are made available for public download under a non‑commercial licence.

    Anonymised child-generated data may still be used internally for research or model development only where legally permitted and subject to enhanced protections. Such data is never included in general‑access public corpora.

    7. Sharing of Research Data

    We may publish anonymised research datasets on our public website under a non‑commercial licence. Access requires acceptance of the licence terms and completion of a registration form.

    We may also share anonymised or aggregated datasets with:

    • academic research partners
    • collaborating institutions
    • technical research teams working on model development

    We never share identifiable personal information, learner accounts, email addresses, IP addresses, or any data that could be linked back to an individual.

    Public datasets are licensed for non‑commercial research and educational purposes only. No ownership or interest in the dataset transfers to the downloader. Sub‑licensing and commercial use are not permitted. Publications using a dataset must acknowledge Cambridge University Press & Assessment as the source (as directed on the dataset page). Excerpts of fewer than 100 words may be quoted, and datasets are provided “as is” without warranties or liability, as set out in the full licence. The full licence text is presented at download time and governs your use.

    8. Retention of Research Data

    We retain research data only as long as needed for:

    • reproducible research
    • evaluation of model performance over time
    • system fairness and bias assessment
    • audit and quality‑assurance requirements

    When no longer required, datasets are anonymised further, archived, or securely deleted.

    9. Your Rights and Controls

    You have full control over whether your data is used for research.

    You may:

    • withdraw consent at any time
    • request deletion of identifiable data
    • request that your learner content not be used for future research
    • access your personal data (subject to anonymisation limitations)

    Withdrawing consent does not affect your ability to use the &Improve products.

    To exercise your rights, contact:
    [Insert Data Protection Officer contact]

    Note on previously published anonymised datasets. Once a dataset has been anonymised and made publicly available, it may not be technically feasible to identify and remove an individual’s prior contributions from copies already downloaded by third parties. We will, however, apply your future preferences to any subsequent dataset releases.

    10. Changes to This Statement

    We will update this statement as our research practices and technologies evolve.

    Whenever changes are made, we will:

    • publish a new version
    • provide a clear summary of the changes
    • update the public version history
    • state the date the new version takes effect
